newsitem.title: USA: Synthetic Industries IPO filing scaled back.
newsitem.headline: Synthetic Industries IPO filing scaled back.

text.p: The parent company of Synthetic Industries Inc said it no longer plans to sell shares in Synethetic's planned initial public offering.

Synthetic filed in August for an IPO of 7.5 million shares to be sold in an estimated range of $15 to $17 each. Of the shares to be sold, 5.8 million, or about 75 percent, were to be sold by parent company Synthetic Industries LP. The company itself was to sell 1.7 million shares.

The company's registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has been amended. Now, a stake of about 35 percent, or 3.3 million shares, will be sold with all shares to be sold by Synthetic Industries Inc.
The estimated price range has not changed.

The company has applied to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol "SINT". Proceeds will be used to repay certain outstanding bank debt. The lead underwriter is Bear Stearns, which said the deal is tentatively scheduled for late September or early October.
Synthetic Industries is a leading producer of polyprolylene fabrics and fibers for the home furnishing, construction, environmental, recreational and agricultural industries.
